blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) on Tuesday criticized Executive Order No. 130, a new class suspension policy, calling it a “band-aid solution” that burdens educators. This followed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s signing of the order on Oct. 28, which allows schools to independently suspend or resume face-to-face classes in coordination with local chief executives (LCEs). In a statement on Tuesday, ACT chairperson Ruby Bernardo said the government should not leave school officials and teachers to handle public safety during disasters.
